subject: Critical Thinking
title: Consequentialism's Blind Spot: Can Good Intentions Produce Evil?
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Consequentialism's Blind Spot: Can Good Intentions Produce Evil?.

hook.text: A doctor secretly kills one healthy patient to harvest organs saving five others. Net utility: positive. Is it ethical?

buildup.text: Consequentialism judges actions solely by outcomes. But this ignores HOW the outcome was achieved — the means matter.

discovery.text: Bernard Williams: 'moral luck' – consequentialism makes morality hostage to outcomes you can't control.

twist.text: A firefighter saves a child. The same child grows up to be a dictator. Was the rescue wrong?

climax.text: The lesson: outcomes matter, but they can't be the ONLY thing that matters. Process, rights, and character also count.

punchline.text: Good outcomes don't always mean good ethics. How you get there matters.

quiz.question: What is 'moral luck' in consequentialist ethics?
options: The morality of an action depends on unforeseeable outcomes, making ethics hostage to chance

details.summary: Consequentialism judges actions by outcomes, but good intentions can produce terrible results. This blind spot reveals how focusing only on consequences ignores the moral significance of motives and processes.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding this gap prevents well-meaning policies from causing harm and encourages humility about predicting complex outcomes.
takeaways: Good intentions do not guarantee good outcomes
Moral theories must account for both intent and consequences

faq.question: Can a policy with good intentions be morally wrong under consequentialism?
faq.answer: Yes, if it produces net harm. Consequentialism only cares about results, so a well-intentioned policy that causes widespread suffering is judged as wrong.

faq.question: How can good intentions lead to evil outcomes in practice?
faq.answer: Complex systems produce unintended consequences. Foreign aid can entrench corrupt regimes, and prohibition can fuel organized crime, despite benevolent motivations.
